subject: SKU consolidation + list-price floor for Azure private offer

Subject: Proposal: SKU consolidation and passback pricing for Azure private offer

Hi Lauren / Ben,

Thanks again for the call today. Attached is a first pass SKU matrix showing our proposed consolidation — Acme would like to move from 14 SKUs to 3 (Core, Performance, Enterprise) to simplify marketplace listing and downstream billing.

High-level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood support a single "bundled SKU" in the Azure private offer flow while preserving partner passback to our reseller network?
- We need visibility on the list-price floor behavior and whether a passback percentage can be preserved within the private offer so our resellers keep their margins.
- Target launch: early January. We expect first-year commit $1.1M USD.

I attached sku_matrix_v1.xlsx. Please confirm if a price-floor (list price minimum) is required by your marketplace listing flow and what typical channel margin ranges you recommend for Azure private offers.

If useful, happy to set a short call next week to run through the matrix.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Acme Cloud Solutions

Subject: Re: Proposal: SKU consolidation and passback pricing for Azure private offer

Sanjay — thanks for the matrix and the clear asks. High level answers up front: yes, we can support a bundled SKU in Azure private offers; the only constraint is how the marketplace enforces list-price floors when passback is required.

A few clarifying Qs so we can model economics:
- Are the three SKUs meant to be per-seat, per-instance, or usage-metered? That affects our metering mapping in the PO.
- Expected blended ASP (list price) for each SKU? If you can give a range (low/expected/high) we will run channel margin scenarios.
- Do you plan to pay reseller commissions on list price or on net revenue after Redwood passback charges?

Proposed packaging options from our side (short):
1) Consolidated bundle (single SKU per tier) — simplest for your billing + preferred by ISVs; requires setting a list-price floor on the private offer to maintain consistent passback.
2) Aggregated metering (multiple internal usage SKUs aggregated to a single marketplace SKU) — more flexible but requires additional mapping work and monthly reconciliation.

I attached our internal pricing playbook excerpt that explains how list-price floors and passback interact for Azure private offers. See pricing_playbook.pdf (redwood_pricing_playbook, page 6 covers passback).

We'd like to propose a short internal sync (30m) next Tue to run scenarios — Karthik / Ben, can you join?

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop

Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Proposal: SKU consolidation and passback pricing for Azure private offer

Internal note / proposed approach — forwarding Sanjay's matrix below. Key points I want us aligned on before we respond with price bands: 

1) Channel margin target: Acme's reseller network expects ~15-20% effective margin on list price. To keep room for reseller promotions and not erode their economics, recommend we plan for a 17.5% gross passback to the reseller in year 1. That leaves room to absorb temporary promotions and still meet partner expectations.

2) List-price floor: The Azure private offer flow (and marketplace reporting) will enforce list-price floors if there is a passback rule. If we set the floor too close to our internal net price, resellers see almost no margin. I recommend a list-price floor at ~1.12x our internal unit cost (or stated differently, roughly 8-12% cushion above our net to preserve margin).

3) Bundling tradeoffs: Single bundle simplifies procurement and reduces SKU maintenance, but it increases the risk of over-discounting in renewals. For a first year launch, propose a hybrid: two bundles (Core + Enterprise) where Performance is an add-on metered SKU. This gives Acme simple procurement while preserving flexibility.

Action items for Karthik / Ben:
- Karthik: run model with channel margin at 15% / 17.5% / 20% and show net to Redwood at each band plus estimated marketplace fees.
- Ben: document operational steps to keep passback intact in the Azure PO (routing, reseller IDs, reporting cadence).
- We'll propose the hybrid to Acme with sample list prices and a DocuSign link for TOC.

Thanks — can you both share a draft model by EOD Wed?

— Lauren

Sanjay — apologies for the slight delay, appreciate the matrix. We reviewed internally and propose the following redline as a starting point: 

- Packaging: Hybrid approach — two listed bundles (Core, Enterprise) + one metered add-on (Performance). This reduces SKU count for procurement while allowing upsell.
- List-price floor: Set per-bundle list price floor (no lower than $9,500 for Core and $28,500 for Enterprise) in the private offer. These floors are intended to prevent parity-breaking discounts while allowing Acme's resellers to take their commissions.
- Channel margin (reseller passback): 16% of list price in year 1; 14% in year 2 (step-down) with a renewal review clause.
- Marketplace fees & Redwood passback handling: Redwood will apply marketplace transaction fees as usual (Azure fee schedule). We modelled expected net to Redwood for your $1.1M commit under these bands and included a shared workbook link in HubSpot (see related_links).

Next steps: if that structure looks acceptable we can generate a DocuSign TOC with the final SKUs and list floors for Acme procurement to sign. Also looping Ben to confirm the reseller ID mapping and reporting cadence.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
